title: C1035C — Battery Junction Box (BJB) Connector
introduction:
I use this battery junction box reference like an address book: the connector identity gets me to the right entry, the drawing shows the numbered terminal, and the assignment table connects that label to circuit information. Start with CNumber and Description, then compare the drawing with the Cavity column. Read across the relevant row for its circuit, color, gauge, function and terminal information.

The part-information table beneath the drawing is separate from the terminal details in the assignment table. Keep those labels distinct; a part reference is not automatically a replacement instruction. Gauge conventions and the meanings of Box, Cols, Size and Used are not explained here, and blank Qualifier cells do not explain when each color entry applies. The physical viewing side is also unspecified. This is an identification reference, without access, probing, wire-selection or replacement instructions. A mismatch between the pin-count field and the drawing remains unresolved.

edits.why: I use the numbered terminal and the outline as the visual key to the assignment table. The drawing shows only a single numbered terminal, so the pin-count field cannot be used to invent another cavity or its location.

Follow each row horizontally so its color, circuit and terminal details stay together. Both entries refer to the same drawn cavity but have different colors; treat their applicability as unresolved rather than assuming separate cavities or deciding that the wires share a connection.
